reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage as a way to earn money through paid program upgrades, displayed profit figures, partner and team growth, and personal referral links. The title explicitly frames the content as how to work on and earn from Forsage, while the demonstrated interface shows tiered upgrade buttons and large earnings associated with multi-person teams, encouraging participation in a recruitment-dependent matrix.

citations.quote: How To Work On Forsage || How To Earn From Forsage

opening.argument: Judge the claims actually presented, not a promise inferred from a dashboard. The title offers to explain how Forsage works and how to earn from it, but it specifies no return or timeframe. The sampled profile displays a profit figure alongside partner and team counts; those figures do not establish what a new viewer would earn. Even the program screen shows an upgrade price, not a guaranteed payout. A viewer should treat these as interface figures requiring scrutiny, rather than as a stated assurance of profit.

citations.quote: How To Work On Forsage || How To Earn From Forsage

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening connects upgrade buttons, team counts and profit figures into a promised earning mechanism. Those elements appear on the interface, but their proximity does not itself explain how profits are calculated or promise that paying for an upgrade will produce them. The title's question of how to earn is broader than a guarantee of earnings.

citations.quote: How To Work On Forsage || How To Earn From Forsage

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explicit guarantee is not needed to identify the promotion. The title presents Forsage as a way to earn, while the displayed interface pairs paid upgrades with personal referral links, partner and team counts, and profit totals. The defense's uncertainty about the precise payout formula does not erase that recruitment-oriented earning presentation.

citations.quote: How To Work On Forsage || How To Earn From Forsage

opening.argument: The most direct description of the video is instructional: its title says "How To Work On Forsage" and "How To Earn From Forsage." The sampled screens show the site's program options and several profiles, including a profile preview. Showing what a platform displays is compatible with an operational walkthrough. The visible figures and links are subjects of that walkthrough; their appearance alone does not show the presenter asking the judge or any viewer to join, buy an upgrade, or expect the same results.

citations.quote: How To Work On Forsage || How To Earn From Forsage

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls the interface an encouragement to participate, but a displayed "Upgrade" control is a feature of the site being shown, not necessarily an instruction from the presenter. Likewise, a profile preview with a personal link and statistics can demonstrate where those fields appear. The cited title establishes an instructional framing; it does not, by itself, establish a solicitation.

citations.quote: How To Work On Forsage || How To Earn From Forsage

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A how-to format can still promote the opportunity it teaches. Here the title specifically offers to teach viewers how to earn from Forsage, and the demonstration repeatedly exposes personal links, profits, partner and team totals, and paid program upgrades. Calling those screens a walkthrough does not account for the earning pitch that organizes what is shown.

opening.argument: The observed interface could be read more narrowly as a program with priced options and referral features. One screen displays a BUSD price to upgrade; profile screens display personal links, partner counts, team counts and profit figures. None of those sampled screens spells out a rule that a viewer's payment funds an earlier participant or that recruiting a particular number of people yields a specified return. Referral links and account statistics are not, on their own, a complete explanation of an abusive compensation mechanism. The judge should not supply that missing rule.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening treats paid upgrades plus large team and profit numbers as proof of recruitment-dependent payouts. The sampled screens do show each element, but they do not state the payout formula or trace a payment from an upgrade to another participant's income. That distinction matters when deciding whether the visible material establishes more than a referral-oriented program.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is not an isolated referral link. The video frames Forsage as a way to earn, while its interface places paid, tiered program upgrades alongside personal links and profiles reporting profits, partners and teams. The defense identifies an unstated payout formula, but that gap does not make this presentation an ordinary loyalty promotion.
